### Main outfits

[![Image 68](https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/f/fb/Misty_SM.png/120px-Misty_SM.png)](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/File:Misty_SM.png)

Misty's main outfit

#### Original series

Misty's first outfit, and her best known, is a yellow crop top and jean shorts held up by red suspenders. Most of her midriff is exposed. She wears red, yellow and white sneakers with it, and carries a red drawstring backpack.

This outfit also debuted her hairstyle, which is typically how she always wears it, regardless of her outfit: a small side ponytail. In [_Pokémon the Series: Sun & Moon_](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_the_Series:_Sun_%26_Moon "Pokémon the Series: Sun & Moon"), Misty holds a [Key Stone](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Key_Stone "Key Stone") on her hairband. She occasionally takes her hair down, but only when she is sleeping, bathing, or wearing a formal outfit of some sort. With her mermaid outfit, she wears her hair down with pearl ornaments.

Misty wore this outfit from _[Pokémon - I Choose You!](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/EP001 "EP001")_ to _[A Date With Delcatty](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/HS11 "HS11")_. She returned to wearing this outfit in _[Alola, Kanto!](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/SM042 "SM042")_.

#### _Ruby and Sapphire_

[![Image 69](https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/b/b1/Misty_AG.png/200px-Misty_AG.png)](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/File:Misty_AG.png)

Misty's [_Ruby and Sapphire_](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_the_Series:_Ruby_and_Sapphire "Pokémon the Series: Ruby and Sapphire") outfit

Misty's second outfit is a yellow sleeveless top or vest with a large blue button on the front and matching shorts, worn over some sort of dark red under-all (swimsuit or leotard, etc.). She wears short pale and burnt orange ankle boots with it. Misty changed bags three times while wearing this outfit. She had her red drawstring bag from her original outfit from _[The Princess and the Togepi](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/AG044 "AG044")_ to _[A Togepi Mirage!](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/AG045 "AG045")_, a [Spheal](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Spheal_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Spheal (Pokémon)")-shaped backpack from _[The Right Place and the Right Mime](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/AG133 "AG133")_ to _[A Real Cleffa-Hanger](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/AG134 "AG134")_, and a pink purse in _[The Mastermind of Mirage Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/The\_Mastermind\_of\_Mirage\_Pok%C3%A9mon "The Mastermind of Mirage Pokémon")_.

Misty wore this outfit from _The Princess and the Togepi_ to _The Mastermind of Mirage Pokémon_.

**Staryu** ([Japanese](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/List_of_Japanese_Pok%C3%A9mon_names "List of Japanese Pokémon names"): **ヒトデマン**_Hitodeman_) is a [Water-type](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Water_(type) "Water (type)")[Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_(species) "Pokémon (species)") introduced in [Generation I](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Generation_I "Generation I").

## Biology

Staryu is a golden-brown, [echinoderm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/echinoderm "wp:echinoderm")[Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_(species) "Pokémon (species)") with faceted skin and five appendages. These appendages surround an exterior organ called the core. The core resembles a golden metal casing with a red gem in the center, which is held in place by a golden ring looped around Staryu's lower left point. Staryu have no jointed limbs to speak of, instead using their psychic powers to move themselves around. If any of Staryu's appendages are lost or eaten by predators like [Lumineon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Lumineon_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Lumineon (Pokémon)"), it is unharmed and can grow them back with ease provided the core is still intact.

When the sun goes down, Staryu's core glows its brightest. Many Staryu will float from the seafloor to the surface and align themselves with stars of the night sky as their core flickers, displaying a connection with the celestial bodies of space. In the [_Pokémon the Series: The Beginning_](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Original_series "Original series") episode _[Bye Bye Psyduck](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/EP091 "EP091")_, it is shown that if Staryu becomes weak, its core will grow faint and flash slowly. During the ends of summer, groups of Staryu tend to gather while lighting up in a steady rhythm. Staryu can be found at the very bottom of the ocean on the [seafloors](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/List_of_Pok%C3%A9mon_by_habitat#Sea_Pok%C3%A9mon "List of Pokémon by habitat"). However, there are times when Staryu finds itself in rivers that lead into the ocean, as seen in [Pokémon Snap](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Snap "Pokémon Snap").

In [An Illustrated Book of POCKET MONSTERS](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/An_Illustrated_Book_of_POCKET_MONSTERS "An Illustrated Book of POCKET MONSTERS") and the original Japanese version of the _Pokémon the Series: The Beginning_ episode _[The Water Flowers of Cerulean City](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/EP007 "EP007")_, Staryu is classified as [hermaphroditic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermaphrodite "wp:Hermaphrodite").

Prior to [Generation IV](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Generation_IV "Generation IV"), Staryu was the [only known Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Signature_move "Signature move") capable of learning the move [Camouflage](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Camouflage_(move) "Camouflage (move)").

## Biology

Staryu is a golden-brown, [echinoderm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/echinoderm "wp:echinoderm")[Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_(species) "Pokémon (species)") with faceted skin and five appendages. These appendages surround an exterior organ called the core. The core resembles a golden metal casing with a red gem in the center, which is held in place by a golden ring looped around Staryu's lower left point. Staryu have no jointed limbs to speak of, instead using their psychic powers to move themselves around. If any of Staryu's appendages are lost or eaten by predators like [Lumineon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Lumineon_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Lumineon (Pokémon)"), it is unharmed and can grow them back with ease provided the core is still intact.

When the sun goes down, Staryu's core glows its brightest. Many Staryu will float from the seafloor to the surface and align themselves with stars of the night sky as their core flickers, displaying a connection with the celestial bodies of space. In the [_Pokémon the Series: The Beginning_](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Original_series "Original series") episode _[Bye Bye Psyduck](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/EP091 "EP091")_, it is shown that if Staryu becomes weak, its core will grow faint and flash slowly. During the ends of summer, groups of Staryu tend to gather while lighting up in a steady rhythm. Staryu can be found at the very bottom of the ocean on the [seafloors](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/List_of_Pok%C3%A9mon_by_habitat#Sea_Pok%C3%A9mon "List of Pokémon by habitat"). However, there are times when Staryu finds itself in rivers that lead into the ocean, as seen in [Pokémon Snap](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Snap "Pokémon Snap").

In [An Illustrated Book of POCKET MONSTERS](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/An_Illustrated_Book_of_POCKET_MONSTERS "An Illustrated Book of POCKET MONSTERS") and the original Japanese version of the _Pokémon the Series: The Beginning_ episode _[The Water Flowers of Cerulean City](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/EP007 "EP007")_, Staryu is classified as [hermaphroditic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermaphrodite "wp:Hermaphrodite").

Prior to [Generation IV](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Generation_IV "Generation IV"), Staryu was the [only known Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Signature_move "Signature move") capable of learning the move [Camouflage](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Camouflage_(move) "Camouflage (move)").

**Starmie** ([Japanese](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/List_of_Japanese_Pok%C3%A9mon_names "List of Japanese Pokémon names"): **スターミー**_Starmie_) is a dual-type [Water](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Water_(type) "Water (type)")/[Psychic](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Psychic_(type) "Psychic (type)")[Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_(species) "Pokémon (species)") introduced in [Generation I](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Generation_I "Generation I").

It [evolves](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Evolution "Evolution") from [Staryu](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Staryu_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Staryu (Pokémon)") when exposed to a [Water Stone](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Water_Stone "Water Stone").

Starmie can [Mega Evolve](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Mega_Evolution "Mega Evolution") into **Mega Starmie** using the [Starminite](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Starminite "Starminite"). Mega Starmie was introduced in [Pokémon Legends: Z-A](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Legends:_Z-A "Pokémon Legends: Z-A").

## Biology

Starmie is an [echinoderm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/echinoderm "wp:echinoderm")[Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_(species) "Pokémon (species)") that resembles two violet [starfish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/starfish "wp:starfish") with faceted skin and five appendages each. The front starfish has a golden formation in the center. In the center of the golden casing is its red jewel core, an exterior organ which can glow in seven colors and has developed to resemble a cut precious stone. The second starfish is semi-attached to the back of the first and can spin 360 degrees. This rotational action is how Starmie swims through the ocean. It can also launch itself out of the water and fly through the air for short periods, as seen in [Pokémon Snap](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Snap "Pokémon Snap").

From its core, Starmie can emit electrical waves that are powerful enough to reach the furthest parts of the universe. The multi-color glowing of its core is also believed to be a method of communication with other members of its species. As seen in the [_Pokémon the Series: The Beginning_](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Original_series "Original series") episode _[The Water Flowers of Cerulean City](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/EP007 "EP007")_, the core will go dark if Starmie is knocked unconscious and will sometimes flicker if Starmie is low on health. Because of its body shape and habit of sending transmissions skyward, some people believe this Pokémon to be [extraterrestrial](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Extraterrestrial_Pok%C3%A9mon "Extraterrestrial Pokémon"). It has been known to cause headaches on people when approached. It is rarely seen in the [wild](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Wild_Pok%C3%A9mon "Wild Pokémon") since it requires an [Evolution stone](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Evolution_stone "Evolution stone") to [evolve](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Evolution "Evolution"), but it can be found in the deepest parts of the [ocean](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/List_of_Pok%C3%A9mon_by_habitat#Sea_Pok%C3%A9mon "List of Pokémon by habitat"). It feeds by absorbing tiny plankton into its body while swimming, and it is preyed on by [Lumineon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Lumineon_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Lumineon (Pokémon)").

### Forms

[![Image 32](https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/c/cb/Friede_Mega_Starmie_Concept_Artwork.png/200px-Friede_Mega_Starmie_Concept_Artwork.png)](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/File:Friede_Mega_Starmie_Concept_Artwork.png)

Reference sheet of Mega Starmie for [_Pokémon Horizons: The Series_](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Horizons:_The_Series "Pokémon Horizons: The Series")

Starmie can [Mega Evolve](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Mega_Evolution "Mega Evolution") into Mega Starmie.

Mega Starmie's elongated limbs and lower body give it a more humanoid appearance, and is also a slightly brighter shade of purple. It adopts humanlike stances and movements thanks to its limbs becoming more flexible, now able to bend its elbows and knees, walk, and sprint. Four prongs on the core's gold casing become longer, resembling an "X". The tips of Mega Starmie's legs are stumpy and somewhat squished, resembling feet. In [_Pokémon Horizons: The Series_](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Horizons:_The_Series "Pokémon Horizons: The Series") and in its official artwork, Mega Starmie's body is shown to be distinctly glossy.

It is unclear whether Mega Starmie’s attempts to imitate [humans](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Human "Human") are done in an effort to communicate with humanity or to supersede it outright. As shown in the [_Pokémon Horizons: The Series_](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Horizons:_The_Series "Pokémon Horizons: The Series") episode _[Roy vs. Friede: Wings of Fire!](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/HZ122 "HZ122")_, it is able to survive the harsh conditions of outer space unassisted. Mega Starmie can rapidly spin its legs and body to charge up its attacks for more power as seen in _[One Step Closer](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/HZ134 "HZ134")_.

## Game data

### NPC appearances

#### In the core series

*   [Pokémon Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Ultra_Sun_and_Ultra_Moon "Pokémon Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon"): A Starmie appears on the northernmost beach on [Route 15](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Alola_Route_15 "Alola Route 15") alongside a [Fisherman](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Fisherman_(Trainer_class) "Fisherman (Trainer class)"). According to the [Trainer](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Trainer "Pokémon Trainer"), the Starmie has been competing in staring contests against various Pokémon for a week. It had most recently beaten a [Corsola](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Corsola_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Corsola (Pokémon)") and [Slowpoke](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Slowpoke_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Slowpoke (Pokémon)") and refuses to leave the beach until it is dethroned. If the [player](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Player_character "Player character") presents a Pokémon that knows [Tickle](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Tickle_(move) "Tickle (move)"), the player's Pokémon will use the move against the Starmie, forcing it to lose the staring contest. The Fisherman gifts the player a [Comet Shard](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Comet_Shard "Comet Shard") for their trouble.

#### In the spin-off games

*   [Pokémon Mystery Dungeon: Gates to Infinity](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Mystery_Dungeon:_Gates_to_Infinity "Pokémon Mystery Dungeon: Gates to Infinity"): Starmie runs the Sunken Treasure mini-game in [Pokémon Paradise](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Paradise "Pokémon Paradise"). In this mini-game, the player collects black, blue and red treasure chests by tilting their Nintendo 3DS. [Chinchou](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Chinchou_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Chinchou (Pokémon)") and rocks appear as obstacles in this mini-game, and touching them deducts one treasure chest, starting with black chests. Unlike Treasure Boxes obtained from dungeons, they are opened upon obtaining. Starmie's mini-game can be played once every in-game day.

**Starmie** ([Japanese](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/List_of_Japanese_Pok%C3%A9mon_names "List of Japanese Pokémon names"): **スターミー**_Starmie_) is a dual-type [Water](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Water_(type) "Water (type)")/[Psychic](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Psychic_(type) "Psychic (type)")[Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_(species) "Pokémon (species)") introduced in [Generation I](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Generation_I "Generation I").

It [evolves](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Evolution "Evolution") from [Staryu](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Staryu_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Staryu (Pokémon)") when exposed to a [Water Stone](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Water_Stone "Water Stone").

Starmie can [Mega Evolve](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Mega_Evolution "Mega Evolution") into **Mega Starmie** using the [Starminite](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Starminite "Starminite"). Mega Starmie was introduced in [Pokémon Legends: Z-A](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Legends:_Z-A "Pokémon Legends: Z-A").

## Biology

Starmie is an [echinoderm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/echinoderm "wp:echinoderm")[Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_(species) "Pokémon (species)") that resembles two violet [starfish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/starfish "wp:starfish") with faceted skin and five appendages each. The front starfish has a golden formation in the center. In the center of the golden casing is its red jewel core, an exterior organ which can glow in seven colors and has developed to resemble a cut precious stone. The second starfish is semi-attached to the back of the first and can spin 360 degrees. This rotational action is how Starmie swims through the ocean. It can also launch itself out of the water and fly through the air for short periods, as seen in [Pokémon Snap](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Snap "Pokémon Snap").

From its core, Starmie can emit electrical waves that are powerful enough to reach the furthest parts of the universe. The multi-color glowing of its core is also believed to be a method of communication with other members of its species. As seen in the [_Pokémon the Series: The Beginning_](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Original_series "Original series") episode _[The Water Flowers of Cerulean City](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/EP007 "EP007")_, the core will go dark if Starmie is knocked unconscious and will sometimes flicker if Starmie is low on health. Because of its body shape and habit of sending transmissions skyward, some people believe this Pokémon to be [extraterrestrial](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Extraterrestrial_Pok%C3%A9mon "Extraterrestrial Pokémon"). It has been known to cause headaches on people when approached. It is rarely seen in the [wild](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Wild_Pok%C3%A9mon "Wild Pokémon") since it requires an [Evolution stone](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Evolution_stone "Evolution stone") to [evolve](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Evolution "Evolution"), but it can be found in the deepest parts of the [ocean](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/List_of_Pok%C3%A9mon_by_habitat#Sea_Pok%C3%A9mon "List of Pokémon by habitat"). It feeds by absorbing tiny plankton into its body while swimming, and it is preyed on by [Lumineon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Lumineon_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Lumineon (Pokémon)").

### Forms

[![Image 32](https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/c/cb/Friede_Mega_Starmie_Concept_Artwork.png/200px-Friede_Mega_Starmie_Concept_Artwork.png)](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/File:Friede_Mega_Starmie_Concept_Artwork.png)

Reference sheet of Mega Starmie for [_Pokémon Horizons: The Series_](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Horizons:_The_Series "Pokémon Horizons: The Series")

Starmie can [Mega Evolve](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Mega_Evolution "Mega Evolution") into Mega Starmie.

Mega Starmie's elongated limbs and lower body give it a more humanoid appearance, and is also a slightly brighter shade of purple. It adopts humanlike stances and movements thanks to its limbs becoming more flexible, now able to bend its elbows and knees, walk, and sprint. Four prongs on the core's gold casing become longer, resembling an "X". The tips of Mega Starmie's legs are stumpy and somewhat squished, resembling feet. In [_Pokémon Horizons: The Series_](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Horizons:_The_Series "Pokémon Horizons: The Series") and in its official artwork, Mega Starmie's body is shown to be distinctly glossy.

It is unclear whether Mega Starmie’s attempts to imitate [humans](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Human "Human") are done in an effort to communicate with humanity or to supersede it outright. As shown in the [_Pokémon Horizons: The Series_](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Horizons:_The_Series "Pokémon Horizons: The Series") episode _[Roy vs. Friede: Wings of Fire!](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/HZ122 "HZ122")_, it is able to survive the harsh conditions of outer space unassisted. Mega Starmie can rapidly spin its legs and body to charge up its attacks for more power as seen in _[One Step Closer](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/HZ134 "HZ134")_.

## Game data

### NPC appearances

#### In the core series

*   [Pokémon Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Ultra_Sun_and_Ultra_Moon "Pokémon Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon"): A Starmie appears on the northernmost beach on [Route 15](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Alola_Route_15 "Alola Route 15") alongside a [Fisherman](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Fisherman_(Trainer_class) "Fisherman (Trainer class)"). According to the [Trainer](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Trainer "Pokémon Trainer"), the Starmie has been competing in staring contests against various Pokémon for a week. It had most recently beaten a [Corsola](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Corsola_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Corsola (Pokémon)") and [Slowpoke](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Slowpoke_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Slowpoke (Pokémon)") and refuses to leave the beach until it is dethroned. If the [player](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Player_character "Player character") presents a Pokémon that knows [Tickle](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Tickle_(move) "Tickle (move)"), the player's Pokémon will use the move against the Starmie, forcing it to lose the staring contest. The Fisherman gifts the player a [Comet Shard](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Comet_Shard "Comet Shard") for their trouble.

#### In the spin-off games

*   [Pokémon Mystery Dungeon: Gates to Infinity](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Mystery_Dungeon:_Gates_to_Infinity "Pokémon Mystery Dungeon: Gates to Infinity"): Starmie runs the Sunken Treasure mini-game in [Pokémon Paradise](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Paradise "Pokémon Paradise"). In this mini-game, the player collects black, blue and red treasure chests by tilting their Nintendo 3DS. [Chinchou](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Chinchou_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Chinchou (Pokémon)") and rocks appear as obstacles in this mini-game, and touching them deducts one treasure chest, starting with black chests. Unlike Treasure Boxes obtained from dungeons, they are opened upon obtaining. Starmie's mini-game can be played once every in-game day.

**Gyarados** ([Japanese](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/List_of_Japanese_Pok%C3%A9mon_names "List of Japanese Pokémon names"): **ギャラドス**_Gyarados_) is a dual-type [Water](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Water_(type) "Water (type)")/[Flying](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Flying_(type) "Flying (type)")[Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_(species) "Pokémon (species)") introduced in [Generation I](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Generation_I "Generation I").

It [evolves](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Evolution "Evolution") from [Magikarp](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Magikarp_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Magikarp (Pokémon)") starting at [level](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Level "Level") 20.

Gyarados can [Mega Evolve](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Mega_Evolution "Mega Evolution") into **Mega Gyarados** using the [Gyaradosite](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gyaradosite "Gyaradosite").

## Biology

[![Image 32](https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/c/ca/Gyarados_Mouth_Closed.png/250px-Gyarados_Mouth_Closed.png)](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/File:Gyarados_Mouth_Closed.png)

Gyarados with its mouth closed

Gyarados is a [piscine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/fish "wp:fish"), draconic [Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_(species) "Pokémon (species)") with a long serpentine body covered in slightly overlapping scales. It is mostly blue with a yellow underbelly, and it has a row of yellow spots down each side. Its mouth is very large and gaping, bearing four pointed teeth and yellow lips. It has one pair of [barbel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/barbels_(anatomy) "wp:barbels (anatomy)") and a small white fin on each side of its face. The barbels are white on a female and blue on a male. It has small, red eyes, a three-pointed, dark blue crest on its head, and four white, spiky [dorsal fins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/dorsal_fin "wp:dorsal fin"). Gyarados's tail fin is similar in structure to the crest on its head, except with a thin, white fin spread between the points.

The process of Evolution causes a change in its brain structure that is believed to cause its violent nature. Gyarados's fangs can crush stones and its scales are harder than steel. Gyarados is feared for its fierce temper and wanton destructive tendencies since ancient times. In some regions, Gyarados is called the "deity of destruction" because of this. It appears in times of conflict and destroys the surrounding area. Its rampages have been known to last a month at a time. These rampages can occur even during a harsh storm. A Gyarados' rage won't stop completely until everything is destroyed. Some believed any human settlement is fated to be destroyed should a Gyarados appear. Gyarados lives in both [fresh and salty waters](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/List_of_Pok%C3%A9mon_by_habitat#Water's-edge_Pok%C3%A9mon "List of Pokémon by habitat"). Both Gyarados and its Mega form have demonstrated in [Pokémon Chronicles](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Chronicles "Pokémon Chronicles") and [_Pokémon the Series_](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_the_Series "Pokémon the Series") that it can leap huge distances both from the water[[1]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gyarados_(Pok%C3%A9mon)#cite_note-1) and from the ground[[2]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gyarados_(Pok%C3%A9mon)#cite_note-2), usually several times its own body length. However, Gyarados is rarely seen in the wild. The move [Hyper Beam](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Hyper_Beam_(move) "Hyper Beam (move)") is often associated with Gyarados due to it being powerful enough to instantly destroy everything it hits.

### Forms

[![Image 33](https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/9/9f/Mega_Gyarados_XY_concept_art.jpg/250px-Mega_Gyarados_XY_concept_art.jpg)](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/File:Mega_Gyarados_XY_concept_art.jpg)

Concept art of Mega Gyarados from [Pokémon X and Y](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_X_and_Y "Pokémon X and Y")

Gyarados can [Mega Evolve](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Mega_Evolution "Mega Evolution") into Mega Gyarados.

When it Mega Evolves, Gyarados becomes bulkier. The fins on its cheeks become longer and gain a yellow tint. Its crest is larger and black, and its barbels also gain considerable length. A large spike extends downward underneath its chin, and it now has a black underside with a red stripe around the edges. The yellow spots along its body are replaced by raised red scales, which propel Mega Gyarados through the water. Two large yellow fins with blue spines appear on its back. Most of the other fins along its back disappear, replaced by two rows of blue spikes. There are now four yellowish, spiky fins near its tail: two on its back and two on its underside.

Due to the stress Mega Evolution puts on a Gyarados's body, it becomes even more ferocious and rough-tempered than before.[[3]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gyarados_(Pok%C3%A9mon)#cite_note-3) All other brain functions cease when Mega Evolution occurs, except for the destructive drive to burn down anything into cinders. Despite its brain having a powerful destructive instinct, it will obey a [Trainer](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Trainer "Pokémon Trainer") it truly trusts. Mega Gyarados can launch at Mach speed by using its orifices to release water from both sides. With this speed, it has enough power to split large ships in two. Mega Gyarados is tied with [Hoopa](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Hoopa_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Hoopa (Pokémon)")[Unbound](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Hoopa_(Pok%C3%A9mon)#Form_data "Hoopa (Pokémon)") as the [tallest](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/List_of_Pok%C3%A9mon_by_height "List of Pokémon by height")[Dark-type](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Dark_(type) "Dark (type)").

**Gyarados** ([Japanese](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/List_of_Japanese_Pok%C3%A9mon_names "List of Japanese Pokémon names"): **ギャラドス**_Gyarados_) is a dual-type [Water](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Water_(type) "Water (type)")/[Flying](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Flying_(type) "Flying (type)")[Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_(species) "Pokémon (species)") introduced in [Generation I](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Generation_I "Generation I").

It [evolves](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Evolution "Evolution") from [Magikarp](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Magikarp_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Magikarp (Pokémon)") starting at [level](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Level "Level") 20.

Gyarados can [Mega Evolve](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Mega_Evolution "Mega Evolution") into **Mega Gyarados** using the [Gyaradosite](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gyaradosite "Gyaradosite").

## Biology

[![Image 32](https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/c/ca/Gyarados_Mouth_Closed.png/250px-Gyarados_Mouth_Closed.png)](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/File:Gyarados_Mouth_Closed.png)

Gyarados with its mouth closed

Gyarados is a [piscine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/fish "wp:fish"), draconic [Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_(species) "Pokémon (species)") with a long serpentine body covered in slightly overlapping scales. It is mostly blue with a yellow underbelly, and it has a row of yellow spots down each side. Its mouth is very large and gaping, bearing four pointed teeth and yellow lips. It has one pair of [barbel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/barbels_(anatomy) "wp:barbels (anatomy)") and a small white fin on each side of its face. The barbels are white on a female and blue on a male. It has small, red eyes, a three-pointed, dark blue crest on its head, and four white, spiky [dorsal fins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/dorsal_fin "wp:dorsal fin"). Gyarados's tail fin is similar in structure to the crest on its head, except with a thin, white fin spread between the points.

The process of Evolution causes a change in its brain structure that is believed to cause its violent nature. Gyarados's fangs can crush stones and its scales are harder than steel. Gyarados is feared for its fierce temper and wanton destructive tendencies since ancient times. In some regions, Gyarados is called the "deity of destruction" because of this. It appears in times of conflict and destroys the surrounding area. Its rampages have been known to last a month at a time. These rampages can occur even during a harsh storm. A Gyarados' rage won't stop completely until everything is destroyed. Some believed any human settlement is fated to be destroyed should a Gyarados appear. Gyarados lives in both [fresh and salty waters](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/List_of_Pok%C3%A9mon_by_habitat#Water's-edge_Pok%C3%A9mon "List of Pokémon by habitat"). Both Gyarados and its Mega form have demonstrated in [Pokémon Chronicles](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Chronicles "Pokémon Chronicles") and [_Pokémon the Series_](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_the_Series "Pokémon the Series") that it can leap huge distances both from the water[[1]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gyarados_(Pok%C3%A9mon)#cite_note-1) and from the ground[[2]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gyarados_(Pok%C3%A9mon)#cite_note-2), usually several times its own body length. However, Gyarados is rarely seen in the wild. The move [Hyper Beam](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Hyper_Beam_(move) "Hyper Beam (move)") is often associated with Gyarados due to it being powerful enough to instantly destroy everything it hits.

### Forms

[![Image 33](https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/9/9f/Mega_Gyarados_XY_concept_art.jpg/250px-Mega_Gyarados_XY_concept_art.jpg)](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/File:Mega_Gyarados_XY_concept_art.jpg)

Concept art of Mega Gyarados from [Pokémon X and Y](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_X_and_Y "Pokémon X and Y")

Gyarados can [Mega Evolve](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Mega_Evolution "Mega Evolution") into Mega Gyarados.

When it Mega Evolves, Gyarados becomes bulkier. The fins on its cheeks become longer and gain a yellow tint. Its crest is larger and black, and its barbels also gain considerable length. A large spike extends downward underneath its chin, and it now has a black underside with a red stripe around the edges. The yellow spots along its body are replaced by raised red scales, which propel Mega Gyarados through the water. Two large yellow fins with blue spines appear on its back. Most of the other fins along its back disappear, replaced by two rows of blue spikes. There are now four yellowish, spiky fins near its tail: two on its back and two on its underside.

Due to the stress Mega Evolution puts on a Gyarados's body, it becomes even more ferocious and rough-tempered than before.[[3]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gyarados_(Pok%C3%A9mon)#cite_note-3) All other brain functions cease when Mega Evolution occurs, except for the destructive drive to burn down anything into cinders. Despite its brain having a powerful destructive instinct, it will obey a [Trainer](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Trainer "Pokémon Trainer") it truly trusts. Mega Gyarados can launch at Mach speed by using its orifices to release water from both sides. With this speed, it has enough power to split large ships in two. Mega Gyarados is tied with [Hoopa](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Hoopa_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Hoopa (Pokémon)")[Unbound](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Hoopa_(Pok%C3%A9mon)#Form_data "Hoopa (Pokémon)") as the [tallest](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/List_of_Pok%C3%A9mon_by_height "List of Pokémon by height")[Dark-type](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Dark_(type) "Dark (type)").

**Brock** (Japanese: **タケシ**_Takeshi_) is an aspiring [Pokémon Doctor](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Doctor_(Trainer_class) "Doctor (Trainer class)") from [Pewter City](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pewter_City "Pewter City") and a former [traveling companion](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Ash%27s_friends "Ash's friends") of [Ash](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Ash_Ketchum "Ash Ketchum"). He used to be the [Gym Leader](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gym_Leader "Gym Leader") of the [Pewter Gym](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pewter_Gym "Pewter Gym"), handing out the [Boulder Badge](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Badge#Boulder_Badge "Badge") to [Trainers](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Trainer "Pokémon Trainer") who defeated him.

Brock journeyed with Ash through the [Kanto](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Kanto "Kanto"), [Johto](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Johto "Johto"), [Hoenn](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Hoenn "Hoenn"), and [Sinnoh](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Sinnoh "Sinnoh")[regions](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Region "Region") in his pursuit of improving his skills as a [Pokémon Breeder](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Breeder_(Trainer_class) "Pokémon Breeder (Trainer class)"). Eventually, he decided to return home and study to become a Pokémon Doctor. In _[Pokémon: To Be a Pokémon Master](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/S25 "S25")_, Brock would reunite and resume traveling with Ash until he decided to head back home.

## In animation

### History

#### Pre-series

[![Image 29](https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/1/1f/Young_Brock.png/220px-Young_Brock.png)](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/File:Young_Brock.png)

A young Brock

Not much is known about Brock's early childhood other than that he grew up at [Pewter City](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pewter_City "Pewter City") in the [Kanto](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Kanto "Kanto") region. In _[Having a Wailord of a Time](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/AG034 "AG034")_, he revealed that his [first Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/List_of_characters%27_first_Pok%C3%A9mon "List of characters' first Pokémon") was an [Onix](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Brock%27s_Onix "Brock's Onix") he received as a tenth-birthday [gift](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gift_Pok%C3%A9mon "Gift Pokémon") from his father [Flint](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Flint_(Kanto) "Flint (Kanto)").

When he was younger, he participated in [Little League Baseball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little_League_Baseball "wp:Little League Baseball"), as mentioned in _[The Little Big Horn](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/EP125 "EP125")_.

Prior to joining [Ash](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Ash_Ketchum "Ash Ketchum") at the end of _[Showdown in Pewter City](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/EP005 "EP005")_, Flint left the family home to pursue his own ventures. As a result, Brock assumed the responsibility of running the [Pewter Gym](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pewter_Gym "Pewter Gym") while also taking care of [his nine younger siblings](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Brock%27s_siblings "Brock's siblings") on his own.

#### [_Pokémon the Series: The Beginning_](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Original_series "Original series")

In _[Showdown in Pewter City](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/EP005 "EP005")_, after Brock awarded Ash the [Boulder Badge](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Badge#Boulder_Badge "Badge"), Flint came forward and confessed who he was. Flint took on the responsibilities of the Pewter Gym and his family, leaving Brock free to [journey](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_journey "Pokémon journey") with Ash and [Misty](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Misty_(anime) "Misty (anime)").

Brock only became the Gym Leader because he felt it was his responsibility, and he admitted to Ash that he would rather [care](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_training#Caretaking "Pokémon training") for Pokémon than [battle](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_battle "Pokémon battle") them. It was his dream to become a great [Pokémon Breeder](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Breeder_(Trainer_class) "Pokémon Breeder (Trainer class)"), and when Flint took back control of the Gym, Brock was allowed to start following this dream.

Brock was also able to meet and make advances towards the many beautiful women he met. At first, he was more casual about approaching women, such as [Officer Jenny](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Officer_Jenny "Officer Jenny") in _[The Water Flowers of Cerulean City](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/EP007 "EP007")_, and more modest as well, such as when he met [Melanie](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Melanie "Melanie") in _[Bulbasaur and the Hidden Village](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/EP010 "EP010")_. However, he became more open and passionate towards almost all single young women as time progressed.

[![Image 30](https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/1/1f/Brock_goodbye_EP083.png/220px-Brock_goodbye_EP083.png)](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/File:Brock_goodbye_EP083.png)

Brock leaving the group to stay with [Professor Ivy](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Professor_Ivy "Professor Ivy")

Brock took care of a [Vulpix](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Brock%27s_Vulpix "Brock's Vulpix") that belonged to a Breeder named [Suzie](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Suzie "Suzie").

Brock briefly left the show during the [Orange Islands saga](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/S02 "S02") to work for [Professor Ivy](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Professor_Ivy "Professor Ivy") on [Valencia Island](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Valencia_Island "Valencia Island") and so is only seen in a couple of cameos in the [second movie](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/M02 "M02"). While there, something happened that will probably remain secret as Brock will only huddle and say "that name" whenever he is asked about it. In the English dub of _[Destiny Deoxys](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/M07 "M07")_, he mentioned his work for her. After this incident, Brock returned to Kanto where he was found by [Delia Ketchum](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Delia_Ketchum "Delia Ketchum"), who helped him to regain his strength. Brock then became a rival to [Mimey](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Mimey "Mimey") until he rejoined Ash and Misty as the three traveled to [Johto](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Johto "Johto").

#### [_Pokémon the Series: Gold and Silver_](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Original_series "Original series")

In _[Beauty and the Breeder](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/EP169 "EP169")_, Brock returned Vulpix to Suzie. Together, they entered Vulpix into the [Pokémon Beauty Contest](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Beauty_Contest "Pokémon Beauty Contest") in [Bonitaville](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Bonitaville "Bonitaville").

At the end of Ash and [his friends](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Ash%27s_friends "Ash's friends")' journey in Johto, the three went their separate ways, with Brock's help requested at home by his father.

#### [_Pokémon the Series: Ruby and Sapphire_](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_the_Series:_Ruby_and_Sapphire "Pokémon the Series: Ruby and Sapphire")

[![Image 31](https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/f/f3/Brock_family.png/220px-Brock_family.png)](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/File:Brock_family.png)

Brock's family

Upon his return home, Brock was dismayed to find that his mother had returned and commandeered the Gym, turning the Rock-type haven into a brightly decorated [Water-type](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Water_(type) "Water (type)") den. Brock battled her for the honor of Rock types and won, promising his brother [Forrest](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Forrest "Forrest") that he would become Gym Leader someday. After getting some new clothes from his mother, Brock set off on a new journey as he goes to [Hoenn](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Hoenn "Hoenn") region in the hopes of finding Ash there.

[![Image 32](https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/a/a4/Brock_AG156_ninja.png/220px-Brock_AG156_ninja.png)](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/File:Brock_AG156_ninja.png)

Brock after catching a Pokémon

In _[You Never Can Taillow](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/AG004 "AG004")_, Brock arrived in [Petalburg Woods](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Petalburg_Woods "Petalburg Woods") as he was about to eat some lunch until he saw a [Thunderbolt](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Thunderbolt_(move) "Thunderbolt (move)") attack and hoped it was [Ash's Pikachu](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Ash%27s_Pikachu "Ash's Pikachu") as he rushed over to see. Brock ended up being right as he sees Ash and his new friends [May](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/May_(anime) "May (anime)") and [Max](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Max "Max") in trouble with a group of [Taillow](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Taillow_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Taillow (Pokémon)"). After rescuing them, Brock formally meets May and Max then informs his intentions to travel with Ash again, which he happily accepts. After that, Brock traveled through Hoenn and Kanto [Battle Frontier](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Battle_Frontier "Battle Frontier") with his friends until he decided to return home.

#### [_Pokémon the Series: Diamond and Pearl_](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_the_Series:_Diamond_and_Pearl "Pokémon the Series: Diamond and Pearl")

In _[Two Degrees of Separation!](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/DP002 "DP002")_, Brock arrived in [Sinnoh](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Sinnoh "Sinnoh") through [Claudina](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Claudina "Claudina") as he meet up with Ash. Although he intended to travel with Claudina, Brock changed his mind when he found out that she has a boyfriend and decided to join Ash in his Sinnoh journey. After finding out that another one of Team Rocket's attempt to catch Pikachu got him separate from Ash, Brock joined him in finding the Mouse Pokémon. In the [next episode](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/DP003 "DP003"), Brock meets [Dawn](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Dawn_(anime) "Dawn (anime)"), who was the one who found and saved Pikachu, as she joins him and Ash on their journey.

Near the end of his Sinnoh journey, Brock began to wonder if he was pursuing the same goal that he had been since he set off on his journey. However, after saving a group of Pokémon in _[The Brockster Is In!](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/DP190 "DP190")_, Brock decided to use all the experiences he gained while traveling with Ash to become a [Pokémon Doctor](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Doctor_(Trainer_class) "Doctor (Trainer class)"). Unfortunately, Brock realized that he won't be able to follow Ash to [Unova](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Unova "Unova") to advise him, as he decided to remain in Kanto to study. After parting ways with Dawn and returning to Kanto, Brock parted ways from Ash once again and return home.

Brock made an appearance in [DPS02](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/DPS02 "DPS02"), where it was revealed that, while waiting to attend a Pokémon medical school, he had been studying hard at home as well as helping out at the [Pewter City](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pewter_City "Pewter City")[Pokémon Center](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Center "Pokémon Center"). In the episode, he played a major role in helping [Forrest](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Forrest "Forrest") to officially become the Pewter City Gym Leader when it is revealed that his father never informed the [Pokémon League](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_League "Pokémon League") of the title change.

#### [_Pokémon the Series: Black & White_](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_the_Series:_Black_%26_White "Pokémon the Series: Black & White")

Brock meeting [Cilan](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Cilan_(anime) "Cilan (anime)")

Brock reappeared in a fantasy in _[Expedition to Onix Island!](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/BW087 "BW087")_, when Dawn learned that [Cilan](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Cilan_(anime) "Cilan (anime)") cooks for himself, Ash, and [Iris](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Iris_(anime) "Iris (anime)"). She said this was similar to the way Brock used to for her and Ash before he decided to become a Pokémon Doctor. In addition, he appeared in a fantasy in _[The Dream Continues!](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/BW142 "BW142")_.

Brock appeared in person in [BWS01](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/BWS01 "BWS01"), where it was revealed that he had attended the Pokémon medical school and had been sent to [Johto](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Johto "Johto") to apprentice under a Pokémon Doctor as part of his training. While passing through the town he bumped into [Pokémon Connoisseur](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Connoisseur "Pokémon Connoisseur") Cilan briefly, then encountered him again when Cilan took his [Pansage](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Cilan%27s_Pansage "Cilan's Pansage") to be treated at the town's [Pokémon Center](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Center "Pokémon Center") after it was injured by a [Gyarados](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gyarados_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Gyarados (Pokémon)"). While waiting for it to recover, the two encountered the beginning Trainer [Ayumi](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Ayumi "Ayumi") who was having trouble teaching her [Pikachu](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pikachu_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Pikachu (Pokémon)") to use [Thunderbolt](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Thunderbolt_(move) "Thunderbolt (move)"); Brock was very impressed with Cilan's talents as Cilan helped Pikachu master the move. Later, when the Gyarados that Cilan encountered earlier started to rampage due to being injured by the [hunter](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_hunter "Pokémon hunter")[Amer](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Amer "Amer"), Brock spotted that it was injured, so after Pansage's [Grass Whistle](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Grass_Whistle_(move) "Grass Whistle (move)") put it to [sleep](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Sleep_(status_condition) "Sleep (status condition)"), Brock was able to quickly treat it. Afterwards, the two said goodbye to each other and continued their separate travels, having never learned their names or that [Ash](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Ash_Ketchum "Ash Ketchum") was a mutual friend of theirs.

### Character

[![Image 38](https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/e/e6/Brock_preparing_Pok%C3%A9mon_food.png/220px-Brock_preparing_Pok%C3%A9mon_food.png)](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/File:Brock_preparing_Pok%C3%A9mon_food.png)

Brock preparing [Pokémon food](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_food "Pokémon food")

Prior to joining [Ash](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Ash_Ketchum "Ash Ketchum") on his [journey](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_journey "Pokémon journey"), Brock had become increasingly frustrated and harsh towards challengers as a result of his responsibilities as both the [Pewter City](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pewter_City "Pewter City")[Gym Leader](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gym_Leader "Gym Leader") and the main caretaker for his [nine younger siblings](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Brock%27s_siblings "Brock's siblings"). Even while traveling, he would think of his family, returning home on several occasions like in _[A Family That Battles Together Stays Together!](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/HS01 "HS01")_.

Brock is noticeably mature, wise, and levelheaded, often acting as an older brother and caretaker to the other characters and a voice of reason in disputes. He will usually place others before himself and will support his friends even against his better judgment or at his own expense. Brock always carries books and maps with him, and thus is usually the character who knows where the group is headed and what they can do when they get there. However, in _[Pokémon the Series: Ruby and Sapphire](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon\_the\_Series:\_Ruby\_and\_Sapphire "Pokémon the Series: Ruby and Sapphire")_, this role was mostly taken over by [Max](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Max "Max"), who owned a [PokéNav](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9Nav "PokéNav").

[![Image 39](https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/8/89/Max_Brock_ears.png/220px-Max_Brock_ears.png)](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/File:Max_Brock_ears.png)

Brock being pulled by the ear by Max

He is renowned for his domestic abilities like sewing, vacuuming, and, most notably, cooking, which Ash and the others always enjoy without fail. The capacity of Brock's [Bag](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Bag "Bag") is endless, as seen in _[The School of Hard Knocks](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/EP009 "EP009")_, where it is capable of containing full tea-sets, tables, and cooking utensils. He also carries a lot of other supplies, such as [Potions](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Potion "Potion") and [Pokémon food](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_food "Pokémon food"), though he has to make pit stops in towns so he could restock the group's supplies.

Despite this, all of his maturity and rationality leaves him completely at the sight of a beautiful woman, and he is extremely passionate over the prospect of finding the girl of his dreams, though he is usually never successful in wooing a woman. Despite this, a few women have been known to show interest in him, such as [Wilhomena](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Wilhomena "Wilhomena"), [Temacu](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Temacu "Temacu"), [Natalie](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Natalie "Natalie"), [Lucy](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Lucy "Lucy"), [Holly](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Holly "Holly"), [Autumn](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Autumn_(DP062) "Autumn (DP062)"), [Narissa](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Narissa "Narissa"), [Lizabeth](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Lizabeth "Lizabeth"), and [Olivia](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Olivia "Olivia"). Despite his failures, Brock remains determined to find a girl to start a relationship with, and has indicated several times he would stop traveling with Ash and stay with the girl if this happened. This behavior tends to wear on the nerves of other characters, and Misty and Max have both commonly dragged Brock away from women by his ear. In addition, some of Brock's own Pokémon, most notably [Croagunk](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Brock%27s_Croagunk "Brock's Croagunk"), have attacked him for getting too flirtatious with women. Brock has also been shown to be able to identify when women are actually [cross-dressing](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Cross-dressing "Cross-dressing") men in disguise by having a peculiar lack of attraction to them. He's also able to do the opposite. A significant exception to this is Ash, who in the guise of "[Ashley](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Cross-dressing#Ashley "Cross-dressing")" was able to fool Brock.

[![Image 40](https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/7/79/Brock_and_Nurse_Joy.png/250px-Brock_and_Nurse_Joy.png)](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/File:Brock_and_Nurse_Joy.png)

Brock flirting with Nurse Joy

He also carries a small blue journal containing information on every girl he meets, referring to it in _[The Rise of Darkrai](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/M10 "M10")_ as his "Little Blue Book of Babes". It most recently appeared in _[Heart of Fire! Heart of Stone!](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/SM103 "SM103")_ and featured [Kahuna](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Island_kahuna "Island kahuna")[Olivia](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Olivia "Olivia"). His love of the [Officer Jenny](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Officer_Jenny "Officer Jenny") and [Nurse Joy](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Nurse_Joy "Nurse Joy") family lines, in particular, can be overbearing and embarrassing for his friends. Brock can also tell whether they are real or impostors, as well as make out subtle physical differences between them. This "ability" has been used multiple times in the series.

[![Image 41](https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/d/de/Brock_Boulder_Badge.png/250px-Brock_Boulder_Badge.png)](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/File:Brock_Boulder_Badge.png)

Brock holding a Boulder Badge

Brock was not shown to [battle](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_battle "Pokémon battle") often in spite of his experience as a former Gym Leader, though he happily accepts challenges from girls like [Miki](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Miki "Miki"), [Molly Hale](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Molly_Hale "Molly Hale"), and Olivia. Instead, he tended to advise Ash on battle strategies and keenly watched matches from the sidelines, seeing the knowledge as valuable to understanding a Pokémon in its entirety.

His goals have played a passive role in his development, and Brock's overall role has generally been one as support for other main characters, usually contributing more in terms of wisdom and comedic antics than the action of the series. Unlike other characters, who aspire to achieve and excel in competitive fields like [Pokémon training](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_training "Pokémon training") and [Pokémon Contests](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Contest "Pokémon Contest"), his initial aim to become a great [Pokémon Breeder](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Breeder_(Trainer_class) "Pokémon Breeder (Trainer class)") was a quiet one and thus did not get showcased frequently. Brock's experience with [Vulpix](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Brock%27s_Vulpix "Brock's Vulpix") taught him a lot about conditioning and nutrition, while further knowledge came from raising [Happiny](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Brock%27s_Happiny "Brock's Happiny") and [Bonsly](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Brock%27s_Bonsly "Brock's Bonsly"). He questioned whether he was actually pursuing his dreams like his friends near the end of _[Pokémon the Series: Diamond and Pearl](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon\_the\_Series:\_Diamond\_and\_Pearl "Pokémon the Series: Diamond and Pearl")_, and ultimately decided to become a Pokémon [Doctor](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Doctor_(Trainer_class) "Doctor (Trainer class)") instead.

### Pokémon

[![Image 42](https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/2/23/Brock_party_JN.png/200px-Brock_party_JN.png)](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/File:Brock_party_JN.png)

Brock and some of his Pokémon in [_Pokémon Journeys: The Series_](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Journeys:_The_Series "Pokémon Journeys: The Series")

As [Gym](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gym "Gym") tradition dictated, Brock's first Pokémon, [Onix](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Brock%27s_Onix "Brock's Onix") and [Geodude](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Brock%27s_Geodude "Brock's Geodude"), were [Rock](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Rock_(type) "Rock (type)")[types](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Types "Types"). However, once he was able to leave the [Pewter Gym](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pewter_Gym "Pewter Gym") and go on a [journey](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_journey "Pokémon journey"), he has dedicated himself to learn about how to care for a variety of Pokémon. As he has stated in _[Battling A Cute Drama!](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/DP125 "DP125")_, his philosophy is that the important thing about being a Pokémon Trainer is the [bond](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Friendship "Friendship") between Trainer and Pokémon.

His Pokémon thus tend to be an eclectic mix of types and dispositions. However, all of his Pokémon tend to have strong bonds with Brock and have been shown to be very capable battlers, despite the fact that Brock does not go out of his way to [train](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_training "Pokémon training") his Pokémon. Brock [grooms](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_groomer "Pokémon groomer") not only his Pokémon but also those of his friends with whom he travels.

#### Original series

One of the most distinct features of Brock's first outfit was his green vest, which had four large pockets on the front. He wore this over an orange short-sleeved shirt, along with brown pants and blue and white sneakers. On either side of his belt, which was black with a gold rectangular buckle, he had attached brown belt pockets. With it, he carried a large, blue backpack with a bedroll seen strapped to it at the top.

It is assumed he keeps many supplies in his many pockets, just as he tends to fill his bag with more supplies than it should be realistically able to hold. However, he has never been seen reaching into these pockets, so their contents remain unknown. The numerous pockets in this outfit were seen in all of his outfits.

Brock wore this outfit from _[Showdown in Pewter City](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/EP005 "EP005")_ to _[A Family That Battles Together Stays Together!](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/HS01 "HS01")_.

#### _Ruby and Sapphire_

Brock's second outfit was a brown jacket with an orange collar. Under it, he wore a green undershirt, but he no longer wears a belt. His clothing slightly mirrors that of his game counterpart in Generation III. His shoes are dark blue, and his new backpack is blue but has no bedroll.

Brock wore this outfit from _[A Family That Battles Together Stays Together!](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/HS01 "HS01")_ to _[Home is Where the Start Is!](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/AG192 "AG192")_. In the main series, it was first seen in Brock's comeback episode _[You Never Can Taillow](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/AG004 "AG004")_. This is the only one of Brock's main outfits to not appear outside of its debut series.

#### _Diamond and Pearl_

Brock's third outfit is one step closer to his original series outfit. He wears a vest again, but the colors are reversed. Instead of a green vest and an orange shirt, he wears an orange vest (which also consists of gray) and a green shirt. His new shoes and backpack are still blue, and his backpack does not have a bedroll.

Brock wore this outfit from _[Two Degrees of Separation!](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/DP002 "DP002")_ to [BWS01](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/BWS01 "BWS01"). He returned to wearing this outfit from _[The Arceus Chronicles (Part 2)](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/JNS02 "JNS02")_ to _[Radio Lulled the Mischievous Stars!](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/JN106 "JN106")_.

#### _Sun & Moon_

Brock's fourth outfit looked almost identical to his original outfit. The only difference is his vest, which now has just two pockets instead of the original four. Brock also holds a [Key Stone](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Key_Stone "Key Stone") necklace inside his shirt and was seen without his vest in _[When Regions Collide!](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/SM043 "SM043")_. Brock wore this outfit during his return in _[Alola, Kanto!](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/SM042 "SM042")_ and _When Regions Collide!_. He returned to wearing this outfit in _[Must Be Our Heroes and the Witch!](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/JN139 "JN139")_.

Heart of Stone!](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/SM103 "SM103")_, Brock wore a summer shirt with a blue, green and white pattern, and cream-colored shorts during his visit to [Alola](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Alola "Alola").

#### Sportswear

**Brock** (Japanese: **タケシ**_Takeshi_) is an aspiring [Pokémon Doctor](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Doctor_(Trainer_class) "Doctor (Trainer class)") from [Pewter City](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pewter_City "Pewter City") and a former [traveling companion](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Ash%27s_friends "Ash's friends") of [Ash](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Ash_Ketchum "Ash Ketchum"). He used to be the [Gym Leader](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gym_Leader "Gym Leader") of the [Pewter Gym](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pewter_Gym "Pewter Gym"), handing out the [Boulder Badge](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Badge#Boulder_Badge "Badge") to [Trainers](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Trainer "Pokémon Trainer") who defeated him.

Brock journeyed with Ash through the [Kanto](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Kanto "Kanto"), [Johto](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Johto "Johto"), [Hoenn](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Hoenn "Hoenn"), and [Sinnoh](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Sinnoh "Sinnoh")[regions](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Region "Region") in his pursuit of improving his skills as a [Pokémon Breeder](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Breeder_(Trainer_class) "Pokémon Breeder (Trainer class)"). Eventually, he decided to return home and study to become a Pokémon Doctor. In _[Pokémon: To Be a Pokémon Master](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/S25 "S25")_, Brock would reunite and resume traveling with Ash until he decided to head back home.

## In animation

### History

#### Pre-series

[![Image 29](https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/1/1f/Young_Brock.png/220px-Young_Brock.png)](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/File:Young_Brock.png)

A young Brock

Not much is known about Brock's early childhood other than that he grew up at [Pewter City](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pewter_City "Pewter City") in the [Kanto](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Kanto "Kanto") region. In _[Having a Wailord of a Time](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/AG034 "AG034")_, he revealed that his [first Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/List_of_characters%27_first_Pok%C3%A9mon "List of characters' first Pokémon") was an [Onix](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Brock%27s_Onix "Brock's Onix") he received as a tenth-birthday [gift](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gift_Pok%C3%A9mon "Gift Pokémon") from his father [Flint](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Flint_(Kanto) "Flint (Kanto)").

When he was younger, he participated in [Little League Baseball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little_League_Baseball "wp:Little League Baseball"), as mentioned in _[The Little Big Horn](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/EP125 "EP125")_.

Prior to joining [Ash](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Ash_Ketchum "Ash Ketchum") at the end of _[Showdown in Pewter City](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/EP005 "EP005")_, Flint left the family home to pursue his own ventures. As a result, Brock assumed the responsibility of running the [Pewter Gym](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pewter_Gym "Pewter Gym") while also taking care of [his nine younger siblings](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Brock%27s_siblings "Brock's siblings") on his own.

#### [_Pokémon the Series: The Beginning_](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Original_series "Original series")

In _[Showdown in Pewter City](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/EP005 "EP005")_, after Brock awarded Ash the [Boulder Badge](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Badge#Boulder_Badge "Badge"), Flint came forward and confessed who he was. Flint took on the responsibilities of the Pewter Gym and his family, leaving Brock free to [journey](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_journey "Pokémon journey") with Ash and [Misty](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Misty_(anime) "Misty (anime)").

Brock only became the Gym Leader because he felt it was his responsibility, and he admitted to Ash that he would rather [care](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_training#Caretaking "Pokémon training") for Pokémon than [battle](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_battle "Pokémon battle") them. It was his dream to become a great [Pokémon Breeder](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Breeder_(Trainer_class) "Pokémon Breeder (Trainer class)"), and when Flint took back control of the Gym, Brock was allowed to start following this dream.

Brock was also able to meet and make advances towards the many beautiful women he met. At first, he was more casual about approaching women, such as [Officer Jenny](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Officer_Jenny "Officer Jenny") in _[The Water Flowers of Cerulean City](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/EP007 "EP007")_, and more modest as well, such as when he met [Melanie](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Melanie "Melanie") in _[Bulbasaur and the Hidden Village](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/EP010 "EP010")_. However, he became more open and passionate towards almost all single young women as time progressed.

[![Image 30](https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/1/1f/Brock_goodbye_EP083.png/220px-Brock_goodbye_EP083.png)](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/File:Brock_goodbye_EP083.png)

Brock leaving the group to stay with [Professor Ivy](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Professor_Ivy "Professor Ivy")

Brock took care of a [Vulpix](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Brock%27s_Vulpix "Brock's Vulpix") that belonged to a Breeder named [Suzie](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Suzie "Suzie").

Brock briefly left the show during the [Orange Islands saga](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/S02 "S02") to work for [Professor Ivy](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Professor_Ivy "Professor Ivy") on [Valencia Island](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Valencia_Island "Valencia Island") and so is only seen in a couple of cameos in the [second movie](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/M02 "M02"). While there, something happened that will probably remain secret as Brock will only huddle and say "that name" whenever he is asked about it. In the English dub of _[Destiny Deoxys](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/M07 "M07")_, he mentioned his work for her. After this incident, Brock returned to Kanto where he was found by [Delia Ketchum](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Delia_Ketchum "Delia Ketchum"), who helped him to regain his strength. Brock then became a rival to [Mimey](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Mimey "Mimey") until he rejoined Ash and Misty as the three traveled to [Johto](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Johto "Johto").

#### [_Pokémon the Series: Gold and Silver_](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Original_series "Original series")

In _[Beauty and the Breeder](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/EP169 "EP169")_, Brock returned Vulpix to Suzie. Together, they entered Vulpix into the [Pokémon Beauty Contest](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Beauty_Contest "Pokémon Beauty Contest") in [Bonitaville](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Bonitaville "Bonitaville").

At the end of Ash and [his friends](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Ash%27s_friends "Ash's friends")' journey in Johto, the three went their separate ways, with Brock's help requested at home by his father.

#### [_Pokémon the Series: Ruby and Sapphire_](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_the_Series:_Ruby_and_Sapphire "Pokémon the Series: Ruby and Sapphire")

[![Image 31](https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/f/f3/Brock_family.png/220px-Brock_family.png)](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/File:Brock_family.png)

Brock's family

Upon his return home, Brock was dismayed to find that his mother had returned and commandeered the Gym, turning the Rock-type haven into a brightly decorated [Water-type](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Water_(type) "Water (type)") den. Brock battled her for the honor of Rock types and won, promising his brother [Forrest](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Forrest "Forrest") that he would become Gym Leader someday. After getting some new clothes from his mother, Brock set off on a new journey as he goes to [Hoenn](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Hoenn "Hoenn") region in the hopes of finding Ash there.

[![Image 32](https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/a/a4/Brock_AG156_ninja.png/220px-Brock_AG156_ninja.png)](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/File:Brock_AG156_ninja.png)

Brock after catching a Pokémon

In _[You Never Can Taillow](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/AG004 "AG004")_, Brock arrived in [Petalburg Woods](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Petalburg_Woods "Petalburg Woods") as he was about to eat some lunch until he saw a [Thunderbolt](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Thunderbolt_(move) "Thunderbolt (move)") attack and hoped it was [Ash's Pikachu](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Ash%27s_Pikachu "Ash's Pikachu") as he rushed over to see. Brock ended up being right as he sees Ash and his new friends [May](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/May_(anime) "May (anime)") and [Max](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Max "Max") in trouble with a group of [Taillow](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Taillow_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Taillow (Pokémon)"). After rescuing them, Brock formally meets May and Max then informs his intentions to travel with Ash again, which he happily accepts. After that, Brock traveled through Hoenn and Kanto [Battle Frontier](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Battle_Frontier "Battle Frontier") with his friends until he decided to return home.

#### [_Pokémon the Series: Diamond and Pearl_](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_the_Series:_Diamond_and_Pearl "Pokémon the Series: Diamond and Pearl")

In _[Two Degrees of Separation!](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/DP002 "DP002")_, Brock arrived in [Sinnoh](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Sinnoh "Sinnoh") through [Claudina](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Claudina "Claudina") as he meet up with Ash. Although he intended to travel with Claudina, Brock changed his mind when he found out that she has a boyfriend and decided to join Ash in his Sinnoh journey. After finding out that another one of Team Rocket's attempt to catch Pikachu got him separate from Ash, Brock joined him in finding the Mouse Pokémon. In the [next episode](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/DP003 "DP003"), Brock meets [Dawn](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Dawn_(anime) "Dawn (anime)"), who was the one who found and saved Pikachu, as she joins him and Ash on their journey.

Near the end of his Sinnoh journey, Brock began to wonder if he was pursuing the same goal that he had been since he set off on his journey. However, after saving a group of Pokémon in _[The Brockster Is In!](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/DP190 "DP190")_, Brock decided to use all the experiences he gained while traveling with Ash to become a [Pokémon Doctor](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Doctor_(Trainer_class) "Doctor (Trainer class)"). Unfortunately, Brock realized that he won't be able to follow Ash to [Unova](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Unova "Unova") to advise him, as he decided to remain in Kanto to study. After parting ways with Dawn and returning to Kanto, Brock parted ways from Ash once again and return home.

Brock made an appearance in [DPS02](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/DPS02 "DPS02"), where it was revealed that, while waiting to attend a Pokémon medical school, he had been studying hard at home as well as helping out at the [Pewter City](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pewter_City "Pewter City")[Pokémon Center](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Center "Pokémon Center"). In the episode, he played a major role in helping [Forrest](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Forrest "Forrest") to officially become the Pewter City Gym Leader when it is revealed that his father never informed the [Pokémon League](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_League "Pokémon League") of the title change.

Brock meeting [Cilan](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Cilan_(anime) "Cilan (anime)")

Brock reappeared in a fantasy in _[Expedition to Onix Island!](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/BW087 "BW087")_, when Dawn learned that [Cilan](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Cilan_(anime) "Cilan (anime)") cooks for himself, Ash, and [Iris](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Iris_(anime) "Iris (anime)"). She said this was similar to the way Brock used to for her and Ash before he decided to become a Pokémon Doctor.
